pinnedFiles.reason: Primary change surface: closeable() (line 106) currently accepts only PhaseParked/PhaseStopped; the spec requires it also accept PhaseWaiting, PhaseCompleted, and PhaseProposed. Close() and isHTTPURL() beside it are unaffected but must be read for the full refusal/ship contract.

Existing unit tests encode the current (now-wrong) contract: TestCloseableAcceptsParkedAndStopped, TestCloseableRefusesEveryOtherPhase, TestCloseableRefusalNamesThePhaseAndInstructsStoppingFirst, and TestCloseRefusesAnOrderThatIsNotParkedOrStopped all assert that waiting/completed/proposed are refused. Per the spec's own Test Approach, new per-phase tests belong beside these.

Defines every Phase constant, the phaseOf/entryUpdates maps EventShipped folds through, and IsActive(). Confirms PhaseShipped is terminal and that appending EventShipped from waiting/completed/proposed needs no change here — applyShipped and the phase fold already handle an arbitrary prior phase.

itemsFor() (line 79) switches on order.Phase (PhaseWaiting/PhaseCompleted/PhaseProposed/PhaseParked) to build inbox items. Confirms AC2 (closed order leaves the inbox) is satisfied automatically once Phase becomes PhaseShipped — no separate inbox change needed, but the analyst must verify this reasoning against the real switch.

Supervisor.finishStep() (line 72) switches on Phase to decide whether to commit/push/open a PR; PhaseShipped matches none of its cases. This is the evidence for AC3/AC4 that the supervisor never acts on a closed order again — needed to justify, not just assert, the no-relaunch acceptance criterion.

Supervisor.continuationKind() (line 132) is the other half of the no-relaunch guarantee: it switches on Phase to decide whether to resume/retry an order, and PhaseShipped matches none of its cases. AC4 explicitly asks for a test that ticks the supervisor once after close() — this function is what that test must exercise.

Wires `loom factory close`: factoryCloseCmd's Long text (line 110) currently documents only 'parked or stopped'; runFactoryClose (line 347) calls factory.Closer unchanged. In scope.paths (cmd/loom/cmd/factory*.go) — the Long description likely needs updating even though runFactoryClose itself does not.

TestFactoryCloseRefusesAWrongPhaseInProcess (line 237) currently proves a waiting order is refused end-to-end through the CLI — this assertion is now wrong per the spec and must be replaced with phase-specific in-process coverage (accepted: waiting/completed/proposed; still refused: running/committed/pushed/retrying).
AC explicitly requires the close section (lines 32-36) to name the phases it accepts; it currently says only 'a parked or stopped order'.

Only prior delivery in this bounded context (Factory supervisor — order lifecycle and ledger, ADR-010). No retrospective.md exists for it. Its analysis.md is the precedent for closeable()'s exact refusal wording ('stop it first, or it has already shipped'), the Close/archiveAndRemove sequencing, and the Developer/QA task phrasing this delivery should extend rather than reinvent.

internal/factory/lifecycle_test.go, internal/factory/supervisor_test.go — broader supervisor test suites; not required to analyze this narrow phase-acceptance change.
internal/factory/ledger.go — Entry/Event struct definitions; the event vocabulary needed (EventShipped, EventApproved, etc.) is already visible in replay.go's phaseOf/entryUpdates maps.
